items.title: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type (PolyShell)
items.summary: An unrestricted file upload vulnerability that allows attackers to breach hundreds of e-commerce stores by injecting a malicious loader via a Magento CMS block. CISA added it to its KEV catalog due to active exploitation.

items.title: Unchecked Return Value in Google Brotli (Memory Corruption, DoS, RCE)
items.summary: A vulnerability in Google's Brotli decoder library that could allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt memory, disclose sensitive information, cause denial-of-service, or potentially execute arbitrary code. CISA added it to its KEV catalog.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce
items.summary: Adobe released a security update addressing multiple critical, high, and medium vulnerabilities, including arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation, arbitrary file system write, and security feature bypass. This bulletin includes fixes for CVE-2026-103849 and CVE-2026-92909.

items.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine (BlockStrap)
items.summary: A critical vulnerability (BlockStrap) allowing unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution through a template engine injection. Adobe fixed it in APSB26-153, but a manual patch is required for new installations.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization
items.summary: A critical incorrect authorization vulnerability affecting Adobe Commerce B2B, allowing for potential privilege escalation or security feature bypass. This was addressed as part of APSB26-153.

items.title: Cross-site Scripting (Stored XSS)
items.summary: A stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability addressed in Adobe Security Bulletin APSB26-153.

items.title: Cross-site Scripting (Stored XSS)
items.summary: Another stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability addressed in Adobe Security Bulletin APSB26-153.

items.title: Improper Input Validation
items.summary: An improper input validation vulnerability addressed in Adobe Security Bulletin APSB26-153.

items.title: Cross-site Scripting (Stored XSS)
items.summary: A stored Cross-site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability addressed in Adobe Security Bulletin APSB26-153.

items.title: Vulnerability in Adobe Commerce
items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability addressed in Adobe Security Bulletin APSB26-153.

items.title: Vulnerability in Adobe Commerce
items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability addressed in Adobe Security Bulletin APSB26-153.

items.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine (StyleSmuggler)
items.summary: A zero-day vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers remote code execution, actively exploited in the wild. Adobe released an emergency hotfix (APSB26-146) to address this critical flaw.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce
items.summary: An emergency security update released by Adobe to address CVE-2026-75650, a critical vulnerability leading to arbitrary code execution that was being actively exploited in the wild.

items.title: Incorrect Authorization (Customer Account Takeover)
items.summary: An unauthenticated incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows attackers to switch a customer session to another customer account, leading to account takeover and access to private customer data. CISA added it to its KEV catalog due to active exploitation.

items.title: Adobe patches critical Magento account takeover
items.summary: Adobe released isolated patch files addressing seven vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-71362, a critical unauthenticated customer account takeover flaw with a CVSS score of 9.1.
